event_name: Cotton Mather's Wonders of Invisible World published
significance: Cotton Mather's Wonders of the Invisible World (1693) was the most prominent intellectual defense of the Salem witch trials, defending the court's use of spectral evidence after the executions; the work became the primary target of Robert Calef's rebuttal and has been analyzed as the Salem prosecutorial community's theological self-justification, representing the last major Puritan defense of aggressive witch prosecution.
source_method: Published primary source (Boston, 1693); analyzed in Boyer and Nissenbaum, Salem Possessed (1974) and Norton, In the Devil's Snare (2002)
